There is a flaw with the NES/SNES RF switch (TV connector) the middle pin is not properly connected to the cord. Not a single piece, not soldered, they just "sit" next to each other. So after time the connection gets "fussy".

One thing I do is completely replace that coax cable. The only tools you need are a soldering iron, spare higher quality coax cable, and a precision screwdriver. A de-soldering wick is nice to have. If you don't have one they are easy to make but can be done without.

First remove the 4 precision screws. Now the one I'm working on looks like it's already been messed with. Probably someone trying to fix it without truely knowing what the real issue is.

There is 3 spots you need to de-solder. You'll need to remove and keep the connector from the original cord for the new one. Also keep the cord to size up the new one.

Once you get the connector on the new cord you're ready to re-solder the connector back to the board. Replace the case, and if everything went well you'll have a RF switch that will out last your NES.
